Split into four children: three new lemmas plus one comparator-accepted declaration reused by name with a byte-identical frozen type. The supplied proof (steps 1–12) contains three independent heavy blocks; each becomes a self-contained child, and the remaining glue stays in the parent. The parent keeps its own declared dependencies jacobian (slicing_im_creg_jacobian_identity) and tonelli (slicing_im_creg_lintegral_cons). Those two are not yet accepted, so they cannot be reused as children, and no child needs them.

Its proof also repairs the supplied step 8, which cites Measurable.inner and Measurable.of_eval_matrix; neither is available in the frozen import closure. subproblems.title: Change of variables through an injective Lipschitz–antilipschitz chart
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0, A ⊆ Φ(Ω) Hⁿ-null-measurable, and g : ℝ^P → [0,∞] a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ⌞A. Let D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩), DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w. Then D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, g∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D, and ∫_A g dHⁿ = ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen Ω → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → A ⊆ Φ '' Ω → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → AEMeasurable g ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict A) → NullMeasurableSet (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ AEMeasurable (fun w => g (Φ w)) ((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A)) ∧ ∫⁻ x in A, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫⁻ w in Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A, g (Φ w) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: this child reuses the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables of DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_area_formula-a1.chart_change_of_variables-a1. That node's status is accepted (all proof gates passed; immutable candidate commit 9fc44225b304fca8af9dead3256575ef03818d1e), and its prerequisites are the accepted lpf_raf_local_lipschitz_area and lpf_raf_chart_preimage_null. Its frozen Lean type, title and statement are copied byte-for-byte from that node, so the runtime maps this key onto the accepted checkpoint by Lean name and provisions no new worker. The decomposition of root.slicing-a1.slice_integer_multiplicity-a1.coarea-a1.chart_regular-a1, the parent of slicing_im_creg_box_coarea, made the same reuse under the same key. The proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim. Inside it, "the parent proof" means root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_area_formula-a1, not slicing_im_creg_box_coarea. "The sibling lemma chart_preimage_null" and "the sibling lemma local_lipschitz_area" are the accepted declarations Submission.lpf_raf_chart_preimage_null and Submission.lpf_raf_local_lipschitz_area. Use in slicing_im_creg_box_coarea: this is the area-formula tool of steps 5 and 10 of the parent proof. The bulk child (Submission.slicing_im_creg_box_bulk) applies it to Φ on Ω with A := Φ(S). The slice_area child (Submission.slicing_im_creg_box_slice_area) applies it with n := m to each slice map σ_t on the open slice B_t, with A := σ_t(S′_t).

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is step 4 of the parent proof (area formula for the injective Lipschitz chart Φ_j, transferring integrals over A_j to D_j, with the null-measurability of D_j and the a.e.-measurability of g∘Φ_j from step 1), for a single chart.

1. Φ is injective on Ω (if Φ(w) = Φ(w′) then c|w − w′| ≤ 0) and continuous on Ω (Lipschitz on Ω).
2. (Borel preimages.) For every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) is Borel: the map Φ̃ := Ω.piecewise Φ 0 (Φ on Ω, 0 off Ω) is Borel measurable (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, Φ continuous on the measurable set Ω, the constant continuous on Ωᶜ), and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) = Ω ∩ Φ̃⁻¹(B).
3. (First conclusion.) Choose a Borel B ⊆ A with Hⁿ(A ∖ B) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Then D = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A ∖ B)); the first set is Borel by step 2 and the second is Lⁿ-null by the sibling lemma chart_preimage_null (with Z := A ∖ B). Hence D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
4. (Second conclusion.) Choose a measurable g′ with g = g′ Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. Since A is null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞A(E) = Hⁿ(E ∩ A) for every E (Measure.restrict_apply₀'), so Z′ := {x : g(x) ≠ g′(x)} ∩ A is Hⁿ-null, and by chart_preimage_null Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′)) = 0. For w ∈ D outside Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′) we have Φ(w) ∈ A and g(Φ(w)) = g′(Φ(w)). Since Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. w lies in D (D null-measurable, ae_restrict_mem₀) and outside the null set Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′) (ae_restrict_of_ae), g∘Φ = g′∘Φ Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. Moreover Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞Ω (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable), hence for Lⁿ⌞D (D ⊆ Ω), so g′∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D (Measurable.comp_aemeasurable) and so is g∘Φ (AEMeasurable.congr).
5. (Area formula for Φ on D.) Φ is Lipschitz on Ω, hence locally Lipschitz on Ω (at each point use the neighbourhood Ω itself, self_mem_nhdsWithin). Apply the sibling lemma local_lipschitz_area with Q := P, the open set Ω, D ⊆ Ω (null-measurable by step 3), u := Φ and weight w ↦ g(Φ(w)) (a.e.-measurable by step 4): ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w) = ∫_{ℝ^P} N dHⁿ with N(y) := Σ_{w ∈ D, Φ(w) = y} g(Φ(w)).
6. (Fibres.) N = 1_A·g pointwise. If y ∈ A, then y = Φ(w₀) for some w₀ ∈ Ω (A ⊆ Φ(Ω)); w₀ ∈ D and, by injectivity of Φ on Ω, the fibre {w ∈ D : Φ(w) = y} is exactly {w₀}, so N(y) = g(Φ(w₀)) = g(y) (tsum_eq_single). If y ∉ A, no w ∈ D satisfies Φ(w) = y because Φ(w) ∈ A for w ∈ D; the fibre is empty and N(y) = 0.
7. (Third conclusion.) ∫ N dHⁿ = ∫ 1_A·g dHⁿ = ∫_A g dHⁿ (lintegral_indicator₀, A null-measurable). With step 5, ∫_A g dHⁿ = ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w). ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ is injective and continuous on Ω; Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Borel) is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise).
D = Borel part ∪ preimage of an Hⁿ-null set, null by chart_preimage_null: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
g∘Φ = g′∘Φ a.e. on D (g′ measurable) using chart_preimage_null on {g ≠ g′} ∩ A: a.e.-measurability.
local_lipschitz_area for u := Φ, weight g∘Φ on D ⊆ Ω.
By injectivity the fibre sum equals the indicator 1_A g; lintegral_indicator₀ gives ∫_A g dHⁿ.

subproblems.title: Area formula through Φ composed with an injective C¹ change of variables χ
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P K-Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some K ≥ 0 and c > 0 (c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for w, w′ ∈ Ω). Let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and χ : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ of class C¹ on B and injective on B, with χ(B) ⊆ Ω. Let S ⊆ χ(B) be Borel and ψ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] Borel. Put S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}, where D = fderiv ℝ and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then ∫_{Φ(S)} ψ dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{S′}(y)·ofReal|det Dχ(y)|·ψ(Φ(χ y))·ofReal(JΦ(χ y)) dLⁿ(y), with Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P and Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ.

subproblems.title: Area formula on the slices {y₀ = t} of a straightened chart (B, χ)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝ^{m+1}, and Φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^P of class C¹, K-Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on Ω (c > 0). Let B ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be open and χ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} of class C¹ on B and Λ-Lipschitz on B, with χ(B) ⊆ Ω. Assume |v − v′| ≤ |χ([t,v]) − χ([t,v′])| whenever t ∈ ℝ, v, v′ ∈ ℝ^m and [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B, where [t,v] := (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1}) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)). Let S ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} and g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] be Borel. Put S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S), 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m} and F̃ := 1_{S′}·(y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)). Then for every t ∈ ℝ, with σ_t(v) := Φ(χ([t,v])) and S′_t := {v ∈ ℝ^m : [t,v] ∈ S′}, ∫_{σ_t(S′_t)} g dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃([t,v]) dL^m(v), where H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P and L^m := volume on ℝ^m.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; L^k = volume on ℝ^k; H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; D := fderiv ℝ.
- For t ∈ ℝ and v ∈ ℝ^m, [t,v] := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) is the point (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1}). In Lean, EuclideanSpace.equiv is ofLp and its inverse is toLp 2, so [t,v]_0 = t and [t,v]_{i+1} = v_i hold by simp (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ).
- S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S).
- 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m}.
- F̃ := S′.indicator (y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)).
Fix K, c > 0 and Λ from the hypotheses, and fix t ∈ ℝ. Write e(v) := [t,v], σ(v) := Φ(χ(e v)), B_t := e⁻¹(B) and S′_t := e⁻¹(S′) = {v : [t,v] ∈ B ∩ χ⁻¹(S)}. The claim is ∫_{σ(S′_t)} g dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃(e v) dL^m(v).

Sibling lemma used: area_formula (Submission.lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables), with n := m. Mathlib results used: Lusin–Souslin MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn, ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, LipschitzOnWith.comp and the chain rule HasFDerivAt.comp.

1. (The linear part ι.) Define ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} by ι(z) := [0,z]. Using Fin.cases on the index, ι(z) has component 0 equal to 0 and component j+1 equal to z_j. So ι is linear, checked componentwise, and since ℝ^m is finite-dimensional it is a continuous linear map (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Again componentwise, e(v) = e(0) + ι(v) for every v. Hence e is continuous, and HasFDerivAt e ι v holds for every v (a constant plus a continuous linear map).
2. (Properties of ι.)
(a) ι(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i < m. Compare components. At 0 both are 0. At j+1 the left side is (e_i)_j = [j = i] and the right side is [j+1 = i+1] = [j = i] (Fin.succ_inj).
(b) |ι z| = |z|. By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and Fin.sum_univ_succ, |ι z|² = 0² + Σ_j z_j² = |z|².
Hence |e(v) − e(v′)| = |ι(v − v′)| = |v − v′|, and e is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
3. (Slice sets.) B_t = e⁻¹(B) is open, since B is open and e is continuous. S′ is Borel: χ is continuous on B (C¹ on B), χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0 is Borel measurable (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise), and S′ = B ∩ χ̃⁻¹(S) because χ̃ = χ on B. So S′_t = e⁻¹(S′) is Borel, as e is continuous and hence measurable. Also S′_t ⊆ B_t.
4. (σ is Lipschitz on B_t.) σ = Φ ∘ χ ∘ e, where:
- e is 1-Lipschitz and maps B_t into B;
- χ is Λ-Lipschitz on B and maps B into Ω (χ(B) ⊆ Ω);
- Φ is K-Lipschitz on Ω.
Applying LipschitzOnWith.comp twice, σ is K·(Λ·1)-Lipschitz on B_t, and in particular continuous on B_t.
5. (σ is antilipschitz and injective on B_t.) Let v, v′ ∈ B_t, so [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B. The slice hypothesis gives |v − v′| ≤ |χ(e v) − χ(e v′)|. Since χ(e v), χ(e v′) ∈ χ(B) ⊆ Ω, the antilipschitz bound of Φ then gives c|v − v′| ≤ c|χ(e v) − χ(e v′)| ≤ |σ(v) − σ(v′)|. Hence σ is injective on B_t: if σ(v) = σ(v′), then c|v − v′| ≤ 0 with c > 0, so v = v′.
6. (A_t := σ(S′_t) is Borel, and B_t ∩ σ⁻¹(A_t) = S′_t.) σ is continuous (step 4) and injective (step 5) on the Borel set S′_t ⊆ B_t, and ℝ^m is Polish, so A_t is Borel by Lusin–Souslin. For the set identity, S′_t ⊆ B_t ∩ σ⁻¹(A_t) is clear. Conversely, if v ∈ B_t and σ(v) = σ(v′) with v′ ∈ S′_t ⊆ B_t, then v = v′ ∈ S′_t by step 5.
7. (Area formula for σ.) Apply area_formula with P, n := m, the map σ, the open set B_t (step 3), A := A_t and weight g. Its hypotheses hold:
- σ is Lipschitz on B_t (step 4) and c-antilipschitz on B_t (step 5);
- A_t ⊆ σ(B_t), because S′_t ⊆ B_t;
- A_t is Borel (step 6), hence H^m-null-measurable;
- g is Borel, hence a.e.-measurable.
Its third conclusion together with step 6 gives ∫_{A_t} g dH^m = ∫_{S′_t} g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v)) dL^m(v), where Jσ(v) := √det(⟨Dσ(v)e_i, Dσ(v)e_j⟩)_{i,j<m}. The cases m = 0 and B_t = ∅ are covered uniformly, so no case split is needed.
8. (Derivative of σ.) Φ is C¹, hence differentiable, so HasFDerivAt Φ (DΦ(x)) x for all x. For y ∈ B, χ is differentiable at y because B is open and χ is C¹ on B, so HasFDerivAt χ (Dχ(y)) y. For v ∈ B_t, the chain rule and step 1 give HasFDerivAt σ (DΦ(χ(e v)) ∘L Dχ(e v) ∘L ι) v. Hence Dσ(v) = DΦ(χ(e v)) ∘ Dχ(e v) ∘ ι (HasFDerivAt.fderiv). By step 2(a), Dσ(v)e_i = DΦ(χ(e v))(Dχ(e v)e_{i+1}) for i < m. Therefore Jσ(v) = 𝒥(e v) for v ∈ B_t.
9. (Conclusion.) Compare the integrands pointwise:
- if v ∈ S′_t, then e(v) ∈ S′, and by step 8, F̃(e v) = g(Φ(χ(e v)))·ofReal 𝒥(e v) = g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v));
- if v ∉ S′_t, then e(v) ∉ S′ and F̃(e v) = 0.
So v ↦ F̃(e v) equals S′_t.indicator (v ↦ g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v))). Since S′_t is Borel, lintegral_indicator and lintegral_congr give ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃(e v) dL^m(v) = ∫_{S′_t} g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v)) dL^m(v). By step 7 this equals ∫_{A_t} g dH^m, and A_t = σ(S′_t) is exactly the image set in the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: e(v) := [t,v] = e(0) + ι(v) with ι(z) := [0,z] linear, |ι z| = |z| and ι(e_i) = e_{i+1}; HasFDerivAt e ι v and e is 1-Lipschitz.
B_t := e⁻¹(B) is open; S′_t := e⁻¹(B ∩ χ⁻¹(S)) is Borel (piecewise extension of χ) and S′_t ⊆ B_t.
σ_t = Φ∘χ∘e is Lipschitz (LipschitzOnWith.comp) and c-antilipschitz (slice hypothesis plus antilipschitz Φ) on B_t; A_t := σ_t(S′_t) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin) and B_t ∩ σ_t⁻¹(A_t) = S′_t.
area_formula for σ_t on B_t (n := m): ∫_{A_t} g dH^m = ∫_{S′_t} g∘σ_t·ofReal Jσ_t dL^m.
Chain rule: Dσ_t(v)e_i = DΦ(χ[t,v])(Dχ([t,v])e_{i+1}), so Jσ_t(v) = 𝒥([t,v]); lintegral_indicator identifies ∫_{S′_t} with ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃([t,·]).

subproblems.title: Borel measurability of the straightened slice-Jacobian integrand F̃
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^P of class C¹, B ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} open, χ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} of class C¹ on B, S ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} Borel and g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] Borel. Put S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S) and 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m}, where D = fderiv ℝ and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then F̃ := 1_{S′}·(y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)) : ℝ^{m+1} → [0, ∞] is Borel measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl P) (B : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (χ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl (m + 1)) (S : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞), ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ B → MeasurableSet S → Measurable g → Measurable ((B ∩ χ ⁻¹' S).indicator (fun y => g (Φ (χ y)) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ (χ y) (fderiv ℝ χ y (EuclideanSpace.single i.succ 1))) (fderiv ℝ Φ (χ y) (fderiv ℝ χ y (EuclideanSpace.single j.succ 1)))).det)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; D := fderiv ℝ. Let S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S), 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m} and F̃ := S′.indicator (y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)). Measurable means Borel measurable.

This is step 8 of the parent proof (slicing_im_creg_box_coarea), where F̃ is the integrand handed to Tonelli. No sibling lemma is used. Mathlib results used: ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, measurable_fderiv_apply_const, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply, continuous_inner, Continuous.matrix_det, Measurable.of_eval and Measurable.indicator. Lean note: the frozen import closure has neither Measurable.inner nor a MeasurableSpace instance on Matrix. So inner products are handled through the continuous map (u, u′) ↦ ⟨u, u′⟩ composed with a measurable pair, and the determinant through the entry function in Fin m → Fin m → ℝ.

1. (Measurable extension of χ.) χ is C¹ on B, hence continuous on B (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Let χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0, which is χ on B and 0 off B. It is Borel measurable by ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, since χ is continuous on the measurable set B and the constant 0 is continuous on Bᶜ.
2. (S′ is Borel.) Since χ̃ = χ on B, S′ = B ∩ χ⁻¹(S) = B ∩ χ̃⁻¹(S). This set is Borel because B is open and χ̃ is measurable.
3. (Replace χ by χ̃ in the integrand.) For k < m+1 let a_k(y) := DΦ(χ̃ y)(Dχ(y)e_k), and for i, j < m let M(y)_{ij} := ⟨a_{i+1}(y), a_{j+1}(y)⟩. Put F̂(y) := g(Φ(χ̃ y))·ofReal √det M(y). Only the outer occurrences of χ become χ̃; Dχ(y) is kept. For y ∈ S′ ⊆ B, χ̃(y) = χ(y), so the integrands of F̃ and of S′.indicator F̂ agree on S′. Set.indicator_congr gives F̃ = S′.indicator F̂. By Measurable.indicator and step 2, it suffices to show that F̂ is measurable.
4. (The factor g∘Φ∘χ̃.) Φ is C¹, hence continuous and measurable. χ̃ is measurable (step 1) and g is measurable, so y ↦ g(Φ(χ̃ y)) is measurable.
5. (The vectors a_k.) Fix k. Then y ↦ Dχ(y)e_k is measurable by measurable_fderiv_apply_const, which holds for any map χ between finite-dimensional spaces. Because Φ is C¹, the map (x, u) ↦ DΦ(x)u on ℝ^{m+1} × ℝ^{m+1} is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply with 1 ≠ 0), hence Borel measurable; the product of these second-countable spaces carries the product Borel σ-algebra. Composing it with the measurable map y ↦ (χ̃ y, Dχ(y)e_k) shows that a_k is measurable.
6. (The entries.) The inner product (u, u′) ↦ ⟨u, u′⟩ on ℝ^P × ℝ^P is continuous (continuous_inner), hence measurable. Composing it with y ↦ (a_{i+1}(y), a_{j+1}(y)) shows that y ↦ M(y)_{ij} is measurable for all i, j < m.
7. (Determinant, square root, ofReal.) The map y ↦ (M(y)_{ij})_{i,j} into Fin m → Fin m → ℝ is measurable (Measurable.of_eval, applied twice). The function N ↦ det(Matrix.of N) on Fin m → Fin m → ℝ is continuous, because det is a polynomial in the entries (Continuous.matrix_det applied to the continuous identity); hence it is measurable. So y ↦ det M(y) is measurable. Real.sqrt is continuous and ENNReal.ofReal is measurable, so y ↦ ofReal √det M(y) is measurable. For m = 0 the matrix is empty with determinant 1, and the same argument applies.
8. (Conclusion.) F̂ is the product of the measurable [0,∞]-valued functions of steps 4 and 7, hence measurable (Measurable.mul). By step 3, F̃ = S′.indicator F̂ is measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0 is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise), so S′ = B ∩ χ̃⁻¹(S) is Borel.
On S′ replace the outer χ by χ̃ (Set.indicator_congr) and reduce to measurability of F̂ (Measurable.indicator).
a_k(y) := DΦ(χ̃ y)(Dχ(y)e_k) is measurable: measurable_fderiv_apply_const plus the continuous (x,u) ↦ DΦ(x)u (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply).
Inner products via continuous_inner; entries via Measurable.of_eval; det via Continuous.matrix_det on Fin m → Fin m → ℝ; then √, ofReal, and the product with g∘Φ∘χ̃.
